documents.unit: The AI Lab Notebook (Clarkson Documentation Library) / Faculty Senate
documents.title: AI Course Policies
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule on AI use. It says Clarkson 'suggests' a syllabus paragraph and the Senate made it 'a recommendation instead of a mandate', so the decision is left to instructors.
documents.summary: A teaching-support page saying Clarkson suggests, but does not require, a syllabus paragraph on AI use, following a 2023 Faculty Senate recommendation. It links a crowd-sourced list of example policies and sets no rule on AI use itself.

units.why: The sentence says Clarkson 'suggests instructors provide a paragraph' on student AI use in the syllabus. It is a recommendation (should), addressed to instructors at course start; P09 (AI statement in syllabus) fits, not P04, because it asks for a statement rather than leaving the rule open.
units.anchor: suggests instructors provide a paragraph outlining the specific guidelines for student use of AI

units.why: The template says the Faculty Senate 'endorsed a recommendation to the faculty that they should include a statement in their course syllabi beginning Fall 2023'. This is the origin of the syllabus-statement expectation, so P09, with should modality as it is a recommendation.
units.anchor: should include a statement in their course syllabi beginning Fall 2023
units.frag_end: use of AI-driven tools in the course

units.why: The text notes 'the Senate amended the proposal by making it a recommendation instead of a mandate'. This says the syllabus statement is not required and leaves choices to instructors; P04 (each instructor decides) fits better than P09 because it concerns the non-binding status, not the content.
units.anchor: making it a recommendation instead of a mandate

units.why: The page links a 'crowd-sourced list of policies from various institutions' and an 'optional resource for developing your course policy'. This supports faculty in drafting course policies, so P63; it does not set any rule on AI use.
units.anchor: Additional optional resource for developing your course policy on use of Generative AI

documents.title: AI Resources for Faculty
documents.stance_why: The guide says 'Clarkson does not have an institutional AI policy, instructors are able to determine when and how students should use AI', so it sets no stance and delegates.
documents.summary: A library guide for faculty stating that Clarkson has no institutional AI policy and instructors decide. It recommends stating levels of AI use in syllabi and lists external resources.

units.why: The guide states 'Clarkson does not have an institutional AI policy' and 'instructors are able to determine when and how students should use AI'. This hands the decision to instructors, so P04 with permit modality 'may'; P56 does not fit as no framework exists.
units.anchor: instructors are able to determine when and how students should use AI

units.why: The page says 'Clearly identifying levels of generative AI usage in the syllabus is the best way to maintain consistency'. It recommends levels of AI use in syllabi, so P05 (named levels); P09 also touches syllabi but the distinguishing point here is the levels.
units.anchor: Clearly identifying levels of generative AI usage in the syllabus is the best way
units.frag_end: consistency across assignments for your students

units.why: The guide tells instructors to 'make expectations very clear and prominently displayed for each assignment or course component'. This is a recommendation to communicate AI expectations per assignment, so P09 at course start.
units.anchor: make expectations very clear and prominently displayed for each assignment or course component

units.why: The sentence says 'Defining AI usage levels and providing examples will help students adhere to expectations'. It advises defining levels with examples; P05 fits since it concerns defining usage levels, rather than P09 which asks for any statement.
units.anchor: Defining AI usage levels and providing examples will help students adhere to expectations
units.frag_start: Defining AI usage levels and providing

units.why: The page says 'If you are unfamiliar with generative AI technology, take some time to learn about the tools and how students are using them'. This advises instructors to learn about AI before setting policy, so P63.
units.anchor: take some time to learn about the tools and how students are using them

units.why: Under Curriculum Suggestions the page says 'these suggestions can help you integrate generative AI into your courses'. It recommends and permits integrating AI into assignments, so P35 (redesign around AI) with unit stance encourage; it notes they may not suit higher-level science or math.
units.anchor: these suggestions can help you integrate generative AI into your courses
units.frag_start: Depending on the discipline and specific
units.frag_end: not be as applicable for higher-level science or math courses

notes: Clarkson reportedly has no institution-wide AI rule; instructors decide. The 2025-2026 Student Regulations (614k chars) were fetched but contain no AI mentions, so not listed as a document. No school or CS-department policy found. Clarkson College (a different institution) IT-17 policy in search results was ignored. Library page is mostly external resource links; only the framing prose was coded.
